title: 月夜（今夜鄜州月）
author: 杜甫
intro: Held captive in war-torn Chang'an, Du Fu doesn't write about himself missing his wife — he imagines her, far away, looking at the same moon and missing him. One of the tenderest love poems in Chinese.
analysis: 这是杜甫写给妻子的诗。安史之乱时，他把家人安顿在鄜州，自己去投奔新皇帝，路上被叛军抓到长安。一个月夜，他想念妻子，却不直接写“我想你”，而是想象妻子在想他。第一、二句：今晚鄜州的月亮，妻子只能一个人在房里看了。第三、四句：可怜那些年幼的儿女，还不懂得思念远在长安的爸爸——孩子不懂，更显得妻子一个人的孤单。第五、六句想象妻子望月的样子：夜雾打湿了她的头发，月光照着她的手臂，让她觉得冷。她站得那么久，可见想得多深。最后两句是盼望：什么时候我们才能一起靠在窗帘边，让月光照干两人脸上的泪痕？前面是“独看”，结尾是“双照”，从一个人到两个人，盼团聚的心情就在这对比里。这种“从对方写起”的写法，中国诗歌里常用，读起来格外深情。
analysisEn: Du Fu wrote this for his wife. During the An Lushan Rebellion he left his family in Fuzhou (in today's Shaanxi) and set out to join the new emperor, but was captured by rebels and taken to Chang'an. On a moonlit night there he misses her — yet instead of saying “I miss you”, he imagines her missing him. Tonight, the moon over Fuzhou: she will be watching it alone in her room. The little children, poor things, are too young to understand that they should be missing their father in Chang'an — which leaves her even more alone. Then he pictures her at the window: the scented night mist dampening her hair, the cold clear moonlight on her arms. She has been standing there a long time. The last couplet is a wish: when will we lean together by the thin curtain, and let the moon shine on us both until our tears are dry? The poem begins with her watching “alone” and ends with the moon shining on the “two” of them. Writing from the loved one's side, rather than one's own, is a classic device in Chinese poetry, and here it is deeply moving.
background: Du Fu (712–770) wrote this in autumn 756, while held in rebel-occupied Chang'an. His wife, née Yang, and their children were sheltering in Fuzhou (鄜州, today's Fu County, Shaanxi), some 150 miles to the north.
pronunciation: 鄜 fū（生僻字）；独看 kān（这里押平声韵，读 kān，与“安”“寒”“干”相押）；长安 cháng；云鬟 huán；虚幌 huǎng；泪痕干 gān。
version: 采用通行教材版本，无重要异文。

lines.lit: in her chamber, she alone watches it.
lines.en: she will watch alone from her room.

lines.lit: From afar I pity the little children,
lines.en: From far away I pity our little ones,

lines.lit: who do not yet understand to miss Chang'an.
lines.en: too young to know they should miss their father in Chang'an.

lines.lit: Fragrant mist: cloud-like coiled hair is damp;
lines.en: The scented mist must dampen her coiled hair;

lines.lit: clear radiance: jade-white arms are cold.
lines.en: the clear moonlight chills her pale arms.

lines.lit: When shall we lean by the thin curtain,
lines.en: When will we lean together by the sheer curtain,

lines.lit: shone on as a pair, tear stains dried?
lines.en: and let the moon on both our faces dry the tears?

words.note: 今陕西富县一带，当时杜甫的家人住在这里。
“闺”是女子的卧室，这里指妻子；现代汉语有“闺女”“闺蜜”。
一个人看月亮。“看”在诗里为了押平声韵读 kān。
“怜”是疼爱、心疼，现代汉语有“可怜”“怜爱”。
年幼的儿子和女儿；现代汉语说“孩子们”。
“解”是懂得，现代汉语有“理解”“了解”。
古代女子盘起来的发髻，像云一样蓬松。
像玉一样白的手臂，古代赞美女子的说法。
现代汉语说“靠”；“倚靠”还用。
透光的薄纱帘子；现代汉语说“窗帘”“纱帘”。

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 同一轮月亮照着长安的诗人和鄜州的妻子，把两地的思念连在一起；从“独看”到“双照”，月亮也见证着盼望团聚的心。
imagery.en: The same moon shines on the poet in Chang'an and his wife in Fuzhou, linking them; from “watching alone” to “shining on both”, it carries his hope of reunion.

imagery.name: 泪
imagery.zh: 两人都在流泪，盼望有一天能在月光下一起擦干泪痕。
imagery.en: Both of them are weeping; he longs for a night when the moonlight will dry their tears together.
